description.value: The study investigated cortical-amygdala functional connectivity in individuals with social anxiety disorder and healthy controls during social speech anticipation using three resting-state fMRI scans.

spans.text: Here we investigate changes in cortical-amygdala coupling in SAD during the anticipation of giving a public speech.

value: We hypothesize that compared to a control group, SAD participants are characterized by less effective emotion regulation, reflected by diminished cortical-amygdala connectivity under social stress.
We investigate whether this pattern of connectivity relates to social anxiety symptoms.

spans.text: We hypothesize that compared to a control group, SAD participants are characterized by less effective emotion regulation, reflected by diminished cortical-amygdala connectivity under social stress.

description.value: A parallel-group, longitudinal repeated-measures observational study with three resting-state fMRI runs before, during, and after speech anticipation.

spans.text: Here we investigate cortical connectivity with the amygdala in social anxiety during a realistic and common stressor by applying task-free (resting state; RS) fMRI scans before, during, and after the anticipation of giving a public speech.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to just lie still, eyes closed, without falling asleep. They were told that they would have to give a videotaped public speech judged by a committee, without being given a speech topic.

stimuli.value: No stimuli were presented during the resting-state scans; participants lay still with eyes closed and were instructed not to fall asleep. They were told that they would have to give a videotaped public speech judged by a committee, without being given a speech topic.

spans.text: Participants were instructed beforehand that a task would follow the scanning procedure, but no details were revealed.
